# Trader Sahab — Rules checklist

<!-- Generated by tools/build_rules_docs.py from docs/architecture/rules.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every rule the system follows: what it says, why it exists, the code that enforces it, and how to see it being followed. **270 rules** in 19 areas, as of 2026-10-05.

Companions: [High-Level Design](HLD.md) · [Low-Level Design](LLD.md) · [Knowledge graph](KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH.md)

## How to use this page

- **Read a rule:** click it to open the reason, the enforcing code, the current setting and the check.
- **Tick rules off:** the [interactive rulebook](https://claude.ai/artifact/5VxZ5bHM8b79u2sSUUtWrK) has search, filters and ticks that are saved. The same page is in the repository as [`rules.html`](rules.html); download it and open it in a browser.
- **Run a checklist on GitHub:** open a new issue and pick *Pre-market checklist*, *New strategy checklist* or *Go-live readiness*. Those checkboxes can be ticked in the issue.
- **Change a rule:** edit [`rules.json`](rules.json), run `python3 tools/build_rules_docs.py`, and commit all three files. A test fails if this page is stale or a rule points at code that no longer exists.

## Entry gates

What must be true before the engine opens a position.

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-01</code> <b>Active</b> — An automatic cash entry needs a confidence score (local setup score x Scorecard system multiplier) of at least the bar for the engine's mode at the…</summary>

An automatic cash entry needs a confidence score (local setup score x Scorecard system multiplier) of at least the bar for the engine's mode at the moment of the entry: 60/100 in Live, 0 in Paper. Below it the signal is blocked and logged. Every entry's score is journaled on its trade row, with the bar applied and whether the live bar of 60 would have blocked it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A clean checklist pass means nothing statistically until the system has shown a real edge; the same gate F&O uses. In Paper the owner asked for automatic trades (2026-10-01), and with the live bar every one was blocked, so the paper bar is 0 and the score is kept as evidence instead. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter; backend/config.py:cash_confidence_bar` |
| **Setting** | `RISK.min_confidence_to_trade = 60 (Live); RISK.paper_min_confidence_to_trade = 0 (Paper)` |
| **How to check** | Live: activity kind 'blocked' with 'confidence N/100 below the 60 bar', GET /api/journal/blocked-signals. Paper: trades.confidence_json on each entry (paper_bar_let_through, live_bar_would_block) |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_confidence.py::test_perfect_setup_still_blocked_when_scorecard_fails; backend/tests/test_paper_auto_entries.py::test_live_blocks_below_the_bar_exactly_as_before_and_offers_a_card; backend/tests/test_paper_auto_entries.py::test_paper_enters_below_the_live_bar_and_journals_the_score` |
| **Source** | README §19, §70, §118 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-02</code> <b>Active</b> — The Scorecard's 'Backtest evidence for the live rule set' row fails when net R &lt; 0 with t &lt;= -2 (committed evidence: -0.356R over 201 trades, t =…</summary>

The Scorecard's 'Backtest evidence for the live rule set' row fails when net R &lt; 0 with t &lt;= -2 (committed evidence: -0.356R over 201 trades, t = -3.59). Any failing row sets the multiplier to 0.25x, so confidence tops out at 25 and no automatic entry can pass the bar of 60: every cash entry in Live and every F&O entry. In Paper the cash bar is 0 (ENT-01, README §118), so paper cash entries are taken.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Two years of backtests show the live rule set loses; the gate must know it. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/evaluation.py:backtest_evidence_row + backend/confidence.py:_system_multiplier` |
| **Setting** | `backend/backtest_evidence.json applies_to = {sahab_dimaag, checklist, 5m}` |
| **How to check** | GET /api/journal/summary -> scorecard row 'Backtest evidence for the live rule set' status 'fail' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_backtest_evidence_gate.py::test_with_the_evidence_no_setup_reaches_the_60_bar` |
| **Source** | README §70 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-03</code> <b>Retired</b> — The Varsity checklist no longer decides automatic entries.</summary>

The Varsity checklist no longer decides automatic entries. Its BUY/SHORT signals still reach _try_enter but are always stopped by the evidence gate. The checklist now only describes setups for the review queue and the journal.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Measured every way (§51, §57, §61, §69) and lost every time; owner decision 2026-09-25. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_process_symbol -> _try_enter` |
| **Setting** | `STRATEGY_PARAMS.sahab_dimaag.entry_mode = "checklist"` |
| **How to check** | no 'trade' activity rows except '(…, manual approval)'; checklist_evals keeps growing |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_backtest_evidence_gate.py::test_with_the_evidence_no_setup_reaches_the_60_bar` |
| **Source** | README §75 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-04</code> <b>Active</b> — Backtest evidence grades only the configuration it measured.</summary>

Backtest evidence grades only the configuration it measured. If the live strategy, entry_mode or interval differs, the row reads 'not_enough_data' and stops failing, and the gate could reopen at 0.6x.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Never apply another rule set's verdict to a new one. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/evaluation.py:backtest_evidence_row` |
| **Setting** | `STRATEGY = "sahab_dimaag"; CANDLE_INTERVAL = "5m"` |
| **How to check** | GET /api/journal/summary scorecard row detail |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_backtest_evidence_gate.py::test_evidence_for_a_different_configuration_does_not_grade_the_live_one` |
| **Source** | README §70 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-05</code> <b>Active</b> — System multiplier: all Scorecard rows pass = 1.0; any fail = 0.25; empty scorecard = 0.25; otherwise (no fails, not enough data) = 0.6, so only a…</summary>

System multiplier: all Scorecard rows pass = 1.0; any fail = 0.25; empty scorecard = 0.25; otherwise (no fails, not enough data) = 0.6, so only a local 100/100 can reach 60.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | 0.5 was a permanent cold-start deadlock (100 x 0.5 &lt; 60). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/confidence.py:_system_multiplier` |
| **How to check** | blocked-signal detail shows 'x 0.25 system evidence' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_confidence.py::test_pending_multiplier_lets_a_near_perfect_local_setup_clear_the_bar` |
| **Source** | README §32 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-07</code> <b>Active</b> — At most one entry per stock per day.</summary>

At most one entry per stock per day. A blocked entry gives the count back, the count is rebuilt from today's journal after a restart, and review approvals honour it. An option buy counts on its underlying, in the same count as cash (FNO-09).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | No revenge trades; cut losses in every backtest variant. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trader_brain.py:trader_brain_signal; backend/trading_engine.py:_process_symbol; backend/trading_engine.py:_fno_entry_block_reason; backend/state.py:_rehydrate_entry_counts` |
| **Setting** | `STRATEGY_PARAMS.sahab_dimaag.max_entries_per_day = 1` |
| **How to check** | blocker 'Already took 1 entry today in this stock'; review refusal 'already traded today' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_entries_today_rollback.py::test_blocked_entry_rolls_back_entries_today` |
| **Source** | README §67, issue #22 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-08</code> <b>Active</b> — Entry signals are edge-triggered: BUY/SHORT fires only on the evaluation where long_ok/short_ok flips from false to true, never repeatedly while it…</summary>

Entry signals are edge-triggered: BUY/SHORT fires only on the evaluation where long_ok/short_ok flips from false to true, never repeatedly while it stays true.

The checklist and sizing read only finished candles. Stops, the plan re-check and fills use the live (latest) price.

| | |

A side passes only if all six required items pass: candlestick pattern, stop at S/R, stop >= 1x cost, above-average volume, trend agreement, net R:R >= 1.5. If both long and short pass on one bar, neither is taken.

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-21</code> <b>Active</b> — An entry is blocked if the latest scan marks the stock excluded.</summary>

An entry is blocked if the latest scan marks the stock excluded. A short is also blocked on a long-only stock (a fixed price band, SCN-18) and when SCANNER.allow_shorts is off. The scanner sets no side (SCN-06), so an entry is never refused for disagreeing with the old score: the checklist's own reading picks the side.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Tradability must hold. The old score's side was measured to carry no information (README §37, §52), so it no longer decides the direction (scanner audit rule 3.8, README §115). Until §115 an entry against the scan's side was refused ('scanner favours SHORT for this stock today'). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_entry_block_reason` |
| **How to check** | blocked reason is the exclusion text, 'this stock has a fixed price band, so it is long-only …' or 'shorts are switched off in the scanner settings'; no 'scanner favours …' after README §115 |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_a_real_scan_leaves_both_sides_open_on_every_listed_stock, backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_a_long_only_stock_is_never_shorted, backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_shorts_switched_off_are_refused` |
| **Source** | README §2, §115; docs/research/scanner-audit-2026-09-28.md |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-22</code> <b>Off by default</b> — The manual review queue is off by default.</summary>

The manual review queue is off by default. It is turned on in memory only, so a restart turns it off.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Opt-in override surface; don't silently resume after a restart. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/review_queue.py:ReviewQueue.enabled; backend/app.py:set_review_queue_enabled` |
| **Setting** | `REVIEW_QUEUE.enabled = False` |
| **How to check** | GET /api/review-queue -> enabled |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_no_card_when_it_could_not_be_taken` |
| **Source** | README §64 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-23</code> <b>Active</b> — A review card is offered only when exactly one required checklist item failed, or the checklist passed and only the confidence gate blocked (in Live…</summary>

A review card is offered only when exactly one required checklist item failed, or the checklist passed and only the confidence gate blocked (in Live; in Paper the bar is 0, so such a setup is entered, not carded). It also needs: bar inside the entry window, stock not traded today, a stop and target the price hasn't passed, no other entry block, a size of at least 1 share, and trader_brain.recheck_plan passing at the offer price for every rule but the card's own blocker (the minimum net reward-to-risk of 1.5 and the stop-to-cost floor; a card blocked on reward-to-risk is exempt from the 1.5, one blocked on the cost floor from that floor). When the failed item is reward-to-risk, its R:R after costs at the offer must be at least 1.0; below that the near-miss is held back (journaled as 'withheld' and replayed, never offered or approvable). Cards blocked by any other item are not held to the floor. Every card states what a hit target makes and a stop loses after costs, and the win rate needed to break even, or that none can.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Only put setups in front of the user that could actually be taken. Of 39 replayed R:R cards, all under 1.0, the mean was -0.78R (t -5.42) and 21 of the 25 that hit their target still lost money (#166). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_offer_near_misses, _offer_review; backend/review_queue.py:single_blocker, floor_reason, build_card, ReviewQueue.hold; backend/trading_engine.py:_card_recheck; backend/trader_brain.py:recheck_plan` |
| **Setting** | `REVIEW_QUEUE.min_net_rrr = 1.0` |
| **How to check** | manual_reviews table (status 'withheld' with withheld_reason for a held-back near-miss); activity kind 'review'; Overview page review queue and its 'Held back today' list |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_single_blocker_only_when_exactly_one_required_item_fails; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_an_rrr_card_is_offered_only_at_or_above_the_floor; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_the_floor_leaves_cards_blocked_on_other_items_alone; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_a_card_that_loses_even_at_its_target_says_it_cannot_break_even; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_card_is_not_offered_when_the_live_price_already_fails_recheck_plan` |
| **Source** | README §64, §105, §121, issue #249 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-24</code> <b>Active</b> — Each (stock, side) has one review card at a time per session, remembered across restarts from manual_reviews.</summary>

Each (stock, side) has one review card at a time per session, remembered across restarts from manual_reviews. A pending, approved, rejected or refused card closes it for the day. A card that expired unanswered can be replaced by a later near-miss read on a later bar that came closer: a larger share of its failed item's bar reached (R:R after costs over 1.5, volume over its average, stop over cost, confidence over 60; pattern, S/R and trend count as 0). A held-back near-miss doesn't take the card; the first one per stock and side is journaled.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A setup hovering near the bar all afternoon is asked about once, but the first near-miss no longer takes the day's only card: TCS's 09:50 volume card (0.7x) expired and its 10:35 near-miss at R:R 1.40 was never offered (#166). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/review_queue.py:ReviewQueue.add, _open_for, progress, _roll` |
| **How to check** | manual_reviews rows per session_date: an expired card followed by a later card for the same stock and side |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_one_card_per_stock_side_and_day_and_it_is_journaled; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_a_later_closer_near_miss_replaces_an_expired_card; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_a_volume_miss_that_expired_is_replaced_by_a_closer_rrr_miss; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_no_new_card_unless_the_last_one_expired_and_this_one_is_later_and_closer` |
| **Source** | README §64, §105 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-25</code> <b>Active</b> — A review card expires 300 s after it is offered and can no longer be approved.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Prices move. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:approve_review; backend/review_queue.py:expire_due` |
| **Setting** | `REVIEW_QUEUE.expiry_seconds = 300` |
| **How to check** | card status 'expired' in /api/review-queue |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_expired_card_cannot_be_approved` |
| **Source** | README §64 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-26</code> <b>Active</b> — An approval overrides only the card's blocker and the confidence gate.</summary>

An approval overrides only the card's blocker and the confidence gate. At click time it re-checks market open, the wall-clock entry window, one entry per day, every _entry_block_reason rule, the live price vs stop/target, sizing and liquidity. A card blocked on reward-to-risk is also held to the R:R floor again: its net R:R after costs at the live price, with the card's stop, target and round-trip cost, must be at least REVIEW_QUEUE.min_net_rrr (1.0), or the approval is refused with that number and the offer's in the reason. Cards blocked on any other item are not held to that floor. Every approval is also held to trader_brain.recheck_plan at the live price, as an engine entry is at its fill, except for the card's own blocker: the minimum net reward-to-risk of 1.5 and the stop at least 1x the round trip's cost (a card blocked on reward-to-risk is exempt from the 1.5, one blocked on the cost floor from that floor).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The owner decides one gate; every risk limit still applies. The floor judged the offer's price, and in the minutes before a click the price can move toward the target: over 71 real cards the net R:R fell below its offer value at 45% of the prices seen while the card was open, by more than 0.10 at 16% (#211). An approval used to skip recheck_plan entirely: a volume card approved after the price moved could be taken at a net R:R of 0.28, or 0.10 above its stop at 336 shares for a -2.11R stop-out (#249). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_approve_claimed, _refuse_review; backend/review_queue.py:floor_reason; backend/trading_engine.py:_card_recheck; backend/trader_brain.py:recheck_plan` |
| **Setting** | `REVIEW_QUEUE.min_net_rrr = 1.0` |
| **How to check** | card status 'refused' with reason, and for the floor 'reward-to-risk after costs is N at the live price P, under the queue's floor of 1 (it was M at the offer)' and outcome net_rrr_live; trade note 'Manually approved — overrode …' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_approval_still_obeys_every_risk_limit; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_an_rrr_card_below_the_floor_at_the_live_price_is_refused_and_journaled; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_the_approval_floor_leaves_cards_blocked_on_other_items_alone; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_the_approval_floor_uses_the_cost_the_offer_used; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_an_approval_below_min_rrr_at_the_live_price_is_refused; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_an_approval_inside_the_stop_to_cost_floor_is_refused; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_card_blocked_on_rrr_is_exempt_from_min_rrr_but_not_from_the_cost_floor` |
| **Source** | README §64, §111, §121, issue #249 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-27</code> <b>Active</b> — Every unapproved card, and every near-miss held back by the R:R floor, is replayed once a minute as if approved at the offer: bars that start after…</summary>

Every unapproved card, and every near-miss held back by the R:R floor, is replayed once a minute as if approved at the offer: bars that start after the offer, exit at the first of stop (assumed first on a both-touch bar), target or 15:08 square-off, with real slippage and charges. The result stays provisional until a completed bar settles it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | So the value of the queue, and what the R:R floor costs or saves, accumulates as evidence instead of being assumed. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/review_queue.py:shadow_outcome; backend/trading_engine.py:_update_review_shadows` |
| **Setting** | `SQUARE_OFF_TIME = "15:08"` |
| **How to check** | manual_reviews.shadow_json; 'If approved' column on Overview; the 'Held back today' list and its total |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_stop_is_assumed_first_when_one_bar_touches_both; backend/tests/test_review_queue.py::test_a_held_back_near_miss_is_journaled_once_replayed_and_cannot_be_approved` |
| **Source** | README §68, §105, issue #102 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-28</code> <b>Active</b> — The cash confidence bar is read from the engine's mode at each entry, so a switch to Live restores the bar of 60 for the very next entry.</summary>

The cash confidence bar is read from the engine's mode at each entry, so a switch to Live restores the bar of 60 for the very next entry. Just before the order the mode is read once more: if it is now Live, the live bar is applied again and the order goes to the mode just read. A position opened in Paper keeps its paper flag and is never closed with a real order.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The paper bar of 0 must never let a real order through: a switch to Live during an entry, or a paper position open at the switch, could otherwise put real money behind a setup only the paper bar allowed. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter, _execute; backend/config.py:cash_confidence_bar` |
| **Setting** | `RISK.paper_min_confidence_to_trade = 0; RISK.min_confidence_to_trade = 60` |
| **How to check** | trades.confidence_json.mode equals trades.mode on every engine entry; no live trade row with live_bar_would_block true |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_paper_auto_entries.py::test_a_switch_to_live_restores_the_bar_for_the_next_entry; backend/tests/test_paper_auto_entries.py::test_a_switch_to_live_during_the_entry_cannot_send_a_real_order` |
| **Source** | README §118, #156 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>ENT-29</code> <b>Active</b> — No entry and no review card until the engine's first market scan has finished since it started: until then there is no market bias, no scan row…</summary>

No entry and no review card until the engine's first market scan has finished since it started: until then there is no market bias, no scan row (exclusions, long-only) and no VIX size multiplier for the rules to read. The block is logged as 'waiting for the first market scan since the engine started'.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | After the 2026-10-01 12:19 restart, 23 stocks were evaluated in the 28 s before the first scan finished, with no market filter and no exclusions (#256). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_entry_block_reason` |
| **How to check** | activity kind 'blocked' with 'waiting for the first market scan' right after a restart |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_engine_correctness.py::test_the_first_tick_after_a_restart_does_not_enter_before_the_first_scan; backend/tests/test_engine_correctness.py::test_no_review_card_before_the_first_scan` |
| **Source** | README §122, issue #256 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>RSK-06</code> <b>Active</b> — Daily loss limit, counted per mode: once today's net realized P&amp;L in the engine's current mode is &lt;= -2% of capital (-₹2,000 on ₹1,00,000), no new…</summary>

Daily loss limit, counted per mode: once today's net realized P&L in the engine's current mode is &lt;= -2% of capital (-₹2,000 on ₹1,00,000), no new cash or F&O entries are taken in that mode. A switch to live is refused when Live's own figure is past the limit. Paper and live P&L are separate counters, each rebuilt from today's journal by its trades' mode after a restart. Open positions are not force-closed.

| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Cap one day's damage; net of charges so the limit matches the account. Pooled, a morning's paper profit (+₹1,356) cancelled out an afternoon's real-money loss (-₹3,082, past the limit), and paper losses could refuse Live (#252). |

In live mode, any Kite position the engine isn't tracking blocks new entries in that symbol and blocks switching to live, until it disappears from Kite. The engine never auto-adopts it. An option the engine holds is tracked; an untracked contract blocks option buys on its underlying.

<details>
<summary><code>EXE-08</code> <b>Active</b> — A position carries whether it is real money, set by the order that opened it, and its closing order goes where that says, whatever mode the engine is…</summary>

A position carries whether it is real money, set by the order that opened it, and its closing order goes where that says, whatever mode the engine is in. Before any closing order for a live position, Kite's day book is read: if Kite holds nothing, the position is dropped and no order is sent; if Kite holds less on the same side, the order is cut to Kite's quantity; if Kite holds the other side, no order is sent. With the market closed, every live position still held is checked against Kite every five minutes, so a late-confirmed entry or one whose close kept failing is dropped once Zerodha has squared it off, or reported if Kite still holds it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A restart comes back in Paper and the mode can be switched with a position open; a closing order for a position Kite no longer holds would open a new one the other way. A rejected square-off close followed by Zerodha's MIS square-off left a position 'open, live' in memory, and its stop then sent a real SELL into a flat account (#250). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_exit_position, _live_fill, _verify_live_position, _reconcile_live_while_closed; backend/state.py:_rehydrate_open_positions` |
| **How to check** | After a restart with a live leg open, the live log shows 'A LIVE position is open' at error level |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_live_restart.py::test_a_position_closed_in_kite_while_the_engine_was_down_sends_no_order; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_no_closing_order_is_sent_for_a_position_kite_no_longer_holds; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_close_is_cut_to_what_kite_holds; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_live_entry_confirmed_after_the_close_is_reconciled_with_kite` |
| **Source** | README §98, §121, issue #250 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>EXE-09</code> <b>Active</b> — A fill's bookkeeping happens the moment the position changes, before any journal write: an entry's stop, target, initial risk and position id, its…</summary>

A fill's bookkeeping happens the moment the position changes, before any journal write: an entry's stop, target, initial risk and position id, its place in max_open_positions, an exit giving its slot back, and the daily loss counter. A journal write that fails (a locked database) never raises into the order path: an activity line stays in memory, and a trade row is queued and written again every tick.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | One 'database is locked' on the entry's log line left the APOLLOHOSP short on the 0.8% fallback stop (8100.88 instead of 8071) and uncounted; on the exit row, it leaked the slot and kept a -₹203.58 loss out of the daily limit (#253). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_execute; backend/paper_broker.py:execute_paper_order; backend/state.py:log, record_trade, retry_journal` |
| **How to check** | activity error 'The journal couldn't record the … fill just now'; the row appears in trades on a later tick |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_locked_journal_on_the_entry_log_line_keeps_the_plan_stop; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_locked_journal_on_the_entry_row_keeps_the_plan_and_is_retried; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_locked_journal_on_the_exit_row_still_frees_the_slot_and_counts_the_loss` |
| **Source** | README §121, issue #253 |

</details>

## Exits and square-off

Stops, targets, the 15:08 square-off and the kill switch.

<details>
<summary><code>EXT-01</code> <b>Active</b> — Stops and targets are checked on every 30 s poll for each held symbol.</summary>

Stops and targets are checked on every 30 s poll for each held symbol. Stop = the plan's stop, else 1.5 ATR / 0.8%; target = the plan's target, else 3 ATR / 1.6%. Breach is ltp at or past the level.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Every position must have a bounded loss and an exit. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_check_stop_take` |
| **Setting** | `RISK.atr_sl_multiplier = 1.5, atr_tp_multiplier = 3.0, stop_loss_pct = 0.8, take_profit_pct = 1.6` |
| **How to check** | trades reason 'stop_loss' / 'take_profit' with note 'stop X / target Y' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_restore_open_positions.py::test_a_restored_short_stops_out_when_price_is_past_its_stop` |
| **Source** | README §6 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>EXT-02</code> <b>Active</b> — With a live Kite data session, stops are also checked on every Kite tick (LTP mode, held symbols only).</summary>

With a live Kite data session, stops are also checked on every Kite tick (LTP mode, held symbols only). The tick path can only close positions, and the poll stays as the fallback.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Up to 30 s of unnoticed stop breach was worth ~₹12 per losing trade. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/stop_watcher.py:StopWatcher._on_ticks, sync; backend/trading_engine.py:check_stop_from_tick` |
| **Setting** | `RISK.tick_stops = true` |
| **How to check** | GET /api/stops/status (connected, watching, exits_fired, stale); activity 'Stop watcher connected …' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_stop_watcher.py::test_the_tick_path_never_opens_a_position` |
| **Source** | README §49 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>EXT-03</code> <b>Active</b> — Exactly one thread may close a position: every exit (stop, target, brain exit, square-off, kill switch) claims the symbol first.</summary>

Exactly one thread may close a position: every exit (stop, target, brain exit, square-off, kill switch) claims the symbol first. A second claimant or a flat position sends nothing.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Two closing orders would flip the position instead of flattening it. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_claim_exit, _exit_position` |
| **How to check** | one closing trade row per position_id |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_stop_watcher.py::test_a_second_thread_mid_close_sends_no_order` |
| **Source** | README §49, §65, issue #98 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>EXT-04</code> <b>Active</b> — From 15:08 to 15:30 IST, every tick closes all open cash positions and all F&amp;O positions.</summary>

From 15:08 to 15:30 IST, every tick closes all open cash positions and all F&O positions. Each position is closed on its own: one that fails (a rejected order, or a paper position with no readable price) is logged once and tried again next tick, and the rest of the square-off, the F&O square-off and the 15:08 price record still run. A paper position is never booked without a live price; a live one is still sent to Kite at market.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Beat Zerodha's 15:12 MIS auto square-off (₹50 + GST per order) for closing-auction stocks. One rejected close used to end the loop for every later position, tick after tick (#250), and a missing price booked the paper exit at the entry price (#255). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_tick_impl, _square_off_all, _close_at_market, market_phase` |
| **Setting** | `SQUARE_OFF_TIME = "15:08"` |
| **How to check** | activity 'Square-off time — closing all open positions'; trades reason 'auto_square_off' / 'fno_auto_square_off' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_kill_switch.py::test_square_off_skips_a_position_another_thread_is_already_closing; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_one_rejected_close_does_not_stop_the_rest_of_the_square_off; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_paper_square_off_without_a_price_is_retried_not_booked_at_the_entry; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_a_live_square_off_without_a_price_is_still_sent` |
| **Source** | README §65, issue #78, §121, issues #250, #255 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>EXT-05</code> <b>Active</b> — In checklist mode the only brain exit is the news veto.</summary>

In checklist mode the only brain exit is the news veto. Exits are otherwise the pattern stop, the S/R target and the square-off; score swings don't close positions.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Varsity exits are stop, target and square-off. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trader_brain.py:trader_brain_signal; backend/trading_engine.py:_process_symbol` |
| **Setting** | `STRATEGY_PARAMS.sahab_dimaag.entry_mode = "checklist"` |
| **How to check** | trades reason 'brain_exit' / 'brain_cover' only on news |
| **Source** | README §4 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>EXT-06</code> <b>Off by default</b> — Step trailing stop (after N x R profit, move the stop up 1R at a time) exists but is disabled.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Varsity Futures ch 7; not validated, so off. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_trail_stop` |
| **Setting** | `RISK.trail_after_r = None` |
| **How to check** | no 'Trailing stop moved to …' activity |
| **Source** | README §6 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>EXT-07</code> <b>Active</b> — Kill switch: pause entries, close every cash and F&amp;O position at market, then switch to PAPER only if every close succeeded (otherwise stay live and…</summary>

Kill switch: pause entries, close every cash and F&O position at market, then switch to PAPER only if every close succeeded (otherwise stay live and name the open symbols; an option Kite sold only part of counts as not closed). Every open-phase tick after it closes anything still open, including an entry that was mid-flight, until a pass leaves nothing open; it stops at the day change.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Stopping must not orphan positions or strand a live one. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:stop_and_flatten, _tick_impl` |
| **How to check** | POST /api/control/stop response {closed, failed, paper_mode}; activity 'Kill switch — …' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_kill_switch.py::test_kill_switch_stays_live_when_a_close_fails; backend/tests/test_engine_money_paths.py::test_the_kill_switch_reflatten_is_retried_until_it_succeeds` |
| **Source** | README §65, §121, issue #250 |

</details>

## Costs

Slippage and charges applied to every fill and every test.

<details>
<summary><code>CST-01</code> <b>Active</b> — The stop distance must be at least 1.0x the round-trip cost (0.1663% of price), both on the finished bar and again at the live entry price.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Below 1x a stop-out is worse than 2R by construction (TMPV lost 4.33R in 38 s). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trader_brain.py:_checklist; recheck_plan` |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>CST-02</code> <b>Active</b> · known gap #66 — A paper fill is booked 3 bp against the trade.</summary>

A paper fill is booked 3 bp against the trade. A live fill is booked at the quantity and average price Kite executed. Both are charged Zerodha's intraday tariff, and realized P&L is net of both legs' charges.

| | |
| --- | --- |

| **How to check** | trades table realized (net), realized_gross, charges columns |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_net_pnl_charges.py::test_both_legs_charges_come_off_the_closing_fill` |
| **Source** | README §45, issues #21, #79 |
| **Known gap** | [#66](https://github.com/harshece16/intraday-trading-agent/issues/66) |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>CST-03</code> <b>Active</b> · known gap #66 — The checklist's round-trip cost is derived from config.COSTS at the largest notional the cap allows, not typed in: 0.1663% today.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A hardcoded 0.12% sat 28% under the measured 16.60 bp. |

<details>
<summary><code>CST-04</code> <b>Off by default</b> — F&amp;O legs use the options tariff: flat ₹20 per order, STT 0.15% sell on premium, NSE 0.03553%, stamp 0.003% buy, 18% GST, no slippage.</summary>

F&O legs use the options tariff: flat ₹20 per order, STT 0.15% sell on premium, NSE 0.03553%, stamp 0.003% buy, 18% GST, no slippage. Exits are net of both legs, and a missing entry charge is recomputed.

## Options (F&O)

Options buying. Switched off today.

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-01</code> <b>Off by default</b> — F&amp;O is off by default.</summary>

F&O is off by default. When on, it runs only with Kite credentials, and a real NFO order goes out only when FNO.enabled is true and paper mode is off.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Switching cash equity live must never silently turn F&O on. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_fno_active, _try_enter_fno; backend/fno_instruments.py:available` |
| **Setting** | `FNO.enabled = False` |
| **How to check** | POST /api/fno/enable; GET /api/fno/status; /api/methods F&O title 'OFF' |
| **Source** | README §7 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-02</code> <b>Off by default</b> — Options buying only: a call on a LONG read, a put on a SHORT read.</summary>

Options buying only: a call on a LONG read, a put on a SHORT read. No writing/selling and no futures; the NFO order is BUY to open and SELL to close.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A long option's max loss is the premium paid; short options and futures have unbounded or margin-call risk. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter_fno; backend/kite_broker.py:place_fno_order; backend/fno_risk.py (docstring)` |
| **How to check** | fno_trades is_call; trades reason 'fno_long'/'fno_short' |
| **Source** | README §7 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-03</code> <b>Off by default</b> — At most one open option contract per underlying (an option order Kite hasn't confirmed counts as one).</summary>

At most one open option contract per underlying (an option order Kite hasn't confirmed counts as one). An option buy acts on the edge-triggered entry signal, like a cash entry, and needs confidence >= 60 (so it is blocked today by the evidence gate). Every evaluation, executed or not, is journaled.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Same confidence gate and signal as cash; one position per underlying. It used to read the level-triggered long_ok/short_ok on every tick (#157). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter_fno, _process_fno, _process_symbol` |
| **Setting** | `FNO.min_confidence_to_trade = 60` |
| **How to check** | fno_evaluations table; GET /api/fno/journal |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_a_standing_long_ok_without_a_signal_buys_nothing, backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_the_signal_is_taken_once` |
| **Source** | README §7, §8, §110 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-04</code> <b>Off by default</b> — Contract: expiry 5-35 days out, the nearest monthly by default (weekly only if prefer_weekly and index), and the strike whose |delta| (BSM at a fixed…</summary>

Contract: expiry 5-35 days out, the nearest monthly by default (weekly only if prefer_weekly and index), and the strike whose \|delta\| (BSM at a fixed 20% vol) is nearest 0.45.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Theta decay accelerates hardest near expiry; near-the-money without paying for pure time value. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/fno_instruments.py:nearest_expiry, find_contract; backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter_fno` |
| **Setting** | `FNO.min_days_to_expiry = 5, max_days_to_expiry = 35, prefer_weekly_for_index = False, target_delta = 0.45, risk_free_rate_pct = 7.0, index_underlyings = ["NIFTY", "BANKNIFTY"]` |
| **How to check** | fno_trades expiry, strike, entry_delta |
| **Source** | README §7 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-05</code> <b>Off by default</b> — Lots = floor(20% of the ₹10,000 F&amp;O allocation / (premium x lot size)); 0 lots blocks the trade.</summary>

Lots = floor(20% of the ₹10,000 F&O allocation / (premium x lot size)); 0 lots blocks the trade. Max loss = the whole premium paid.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Decide the maximum loss before placing the trade; ring-fenced capital. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/fno_risk.py:lots_to_buy; backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter_fno` |
| **Setting** | `FNO.capital = 10000.0, max_premium_risk_pct = 20.0` |
| **How to check** | blocked 'premium … too large for the 20.0% of ₹10,000 F&O allocation'; fno_trades lots |
| **Source** | README §7 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-06</code> <b>Off by default</b> — Premium exits: close if the premium falls 40% or rises 80% from the premium paid, checked each open-phase tick whether or not F&amp;O is switched on.</summary>

Premium exits: close if the premium falls 40% or rises 80% from the premium paid, checked each open-phase tick whether or not F&O is switched on. A live position reads Kite's quote; a paper one is a model price, Black-Scholes at the entry volatility on the underlying's live price, read for an index under its quote name (NIFTY as NSE:NIFTY 50 / ^NSEI, BANKNIFTY as NSE:NIFTY BANK / ^NSEBANK). If that price can't be read, nothing fires on that tick.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | An option buyer's P&L is realized in premium terms. The switch is in memory, so a restart turns it off with a restored position still open (#187); NSE:NIFTY is not a Kite instrument, so a paper index option never repriced (#189). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_check_fno_stop_take; backend/trading_engine.py:_paper_fno_premium; backend/trading_engine.py:_process_fno; backend/data_provider.py:kite_quote_key; backend/fno_risk.py:stop_and_target_premium` |
| **Setting** | `FNO.stop_loss_pct_of_premium = 40.0, target_pct_of_premium = 80.0` |
| **How to check** | trades reason 'fno_stop_loss' / 'fno_take_profit' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_paper_fno_stops.py, backend/tests/test_fno_index_quote.py::test_a_paper_nifty_option_reprices_from_the_index, backend/tests/test_fno_restart.py::test_the_restored_option_is_watched_with_fno_switched_off` |
| **Source** | README §7, §98, §110 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-07</code> <b>Off by default</b> — Live F&amp;O entries need a real premium quote (blocked otherwise).</summary>

Live F&O entries need a real premium quote (blocked otherwise). Paper uses the Black-Scholes price at 20% vol.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Never price a live order off a model. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter_fno` |
| **How to check** | blocked 'could not fetch a live premium quote'; fno_evaluations block_reason |
| **Source** | README §7 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-08</code> <b>Off by default</b> — No stock-option buy in a stock on NSE's F&amp;O ban list (Market Wide Position Limit) for the day.</summary>

No stock-option buy in a stock on NSE's F&O ban list (Market Wide Position Limit) for the day. The check runs after the confidence gate and before any contract lookup, quote or order. A list that cannot be read, or is for another trade date, is unknown: stock-option buys are refused and the reason says the status is unknown, and for a list that could not be fetched, when the last try failed and when it is tried again. While it cannot be fetched, the check answers at once until then (SCN-20), not after a timeout per candidate. Index options are exempt.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Increasing a derivative position in a banned stock is penalised (₹5,000 to ₹1,00,000, NISM Series VIII), so an unknown status is not treated as clear. The scanner's guard (SCN-17, SCN-20) reads the same list but lets an unknown list exclude nothing, because a cash trade carries no such penalty. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/fno_risk.py:mwpl_block_reason; backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter_fno; backend/nse_feed.py:fno_ban_list, last_failure` |
| **Setting** | `FNO.enabled = False, index_underlyings = ["NIFTY", "BANKNIFTY"]` |
| **How to check** | activity 'F&O entry signal skipped — In NSE's F&O ban for …' or '… ban status is unknown …'; fno_evaluations block_reason |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_fno_mwpl.py::test_the_engine_refuses_a_banned_underlying_and_journals_why, backend/tests/test_fno_mwpl.py::test_the_engine_refuses_stock_options_when_the_list_is_unknown, backend/tests/test_fno_mwpl.py::test_nse_down_costs_one_timeout_not_one_per_candidate_and_the_reason_says_when` |
| **Source** | README §108, §111; NSE fo_secban.csv |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-09</code> <b>Off by default</b> — An option buy passes the cash entry rules on its underlying, a call counting as a LONG and a put as a SHORT: one entry per stock per day, shared with…</summary>

An option buy passes the cash entry rules on its underlying, a call counting as a LONG and a put as a SHORT: one entry per stock per day, shared with cash; the pause; an untracked Kite position in the stock; the scanner's exclusion and short limits (SCANNER.allow_shorts = False refuses a put); the market bias; the daily loss limit; the open-position cap; and the sector cap, which counts cash and option positions together. An untracked Kite position in any contract on the underlying also blocks it. Not applied: the checklist's re-check of its stop and target at the live price (an option's exits are on the premium) and cash sizing (FNO-05 sizes it).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | With F&O on, the engine could re-enter one underlying all session, stack a sector, and buy calls in a risk-off market (#157). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_fno_entry_block_reason, _entry_block_reason, _spend_entry; backend/fno_risk.py:contract_on; backend/state.py:_rehydrate_entry_counts` |
| **Setting** | `STRATEGY_PARAMS.sahab_dimaag.max_entries_per_day = 1; RISK.max_positions_per_sector = 1` |
| **How to check** | activity 'F&O entry signal skipped — …'; fno_evaluations block_reason |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_one_entry_per_stock_per_day_counts_a_cash_entry_too, backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_market_bias_blocks_calls_in_risk_off_and_puts_in_risk_on, backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_an_open_option_counts_against_the_sector_cap_for_cash_too, backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_an_untracked_kite_position_in_any_contract_on_the_stock_blocks` |
| **Source** | README §110 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-10</code> <b>Off by default</b> — Liquidity gate on the contract's own NFO book, the last check before an option buy: refuse if the spread is over 2% of the mid premium, five levels…</summary>

Liquidity gate on the contract's own NFO book, the last check before an option buy: refuse if the spread is over 2% of the mid premium, five levels can't fill the order, filling it moves the price over 1% from the mid, or either side holds under 3x the order. With no book to read, paper goes ahead (journaled as unchecked) and live is refused.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The option tariff models no slippage, so the cash cap (2x modelled slippage) would refuse every option. A round trip pays about one spread, and 2% of the premium is a twentieth of the 40% premium stop (#157). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/liquidity.py:assess_option, check_option, check; backend/trading_engine.py:_try_enter_fno` |
| **Setting** | `FNO.max_spread_pct_of_premium = 2.0; LIQUIDITY.min_depth_multiple = 3.0` |
| **How to check** | liquidity_checks rows whose symbol is an NFO contract; blocked reason 'liquidity: the option's …' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_assess_option_rules, backend/tests/test_fno_entry_rules.py::test_paper_goes_ahead_without_a_book_and_live_does_not` |
| **Source** | README §110 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-11</code> <b>Off by default</b> — A live option order is booked only from Kite's report of it, as EXE-07 does for cash: the executed premium and quantity, and the premium stop, target…</summary>

A live option order is booked only from Kite's report of it, as EXE-07 does for cash: the executed premium and quantity, and the premium stop, target and maximum loss worked out from the premium paid. A rejected buy books nothing and doesn't spend the day's entry; a rejected sale leaves the position open and watched. A part fill books what filled. An unconfirmed order books nothing, blocks further option orders on the underlying, and is booked when Kite answers. Closing takes a claim, so two threads can't both sell.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Live option P&L would have been the quote's, and a rejected order would have been booked as a position (#186). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_live_fno_fill, _book_fno_entry, _book_fno_exit, _close_fno, _claim_fno_exit, _resolve_unconfirmed_orders; backend/kite_broker.py:KiteExecutor.wait_for_fill` |
| **Setting** | `KITE_FILL_DEADLINE_S = 5; KITE_FILL_POLL_S = 0.25` |
| **How to check** | A live NFO row in trades has order_id and signal_price, and its note gives the slippage in bp against the quoted premium |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_fno_live_fills.py::test_a_live_buy_is_booked_at_kites_premium_and_quantity, backend/tests/test_fno_live_fills.py::test_a_rejected_exit_leaves_the_position_open_and_watched, backend/tests/test_fno_live_fills.py::test_an_unconfirmed_buy_books_nothing_blocks_a_second_and_is_booked_when_kite_answers` |
| **Source** | README §110 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>FNO-12</code> <b>Off by default</b> — On restart, today's open option positions are rebuilt from fno_trades and their legs in trades (the quantity still open, entry charges, premium stop…</summary>

On restart, today's open option positions are rebuilt from fno_trades and their legs in trades (the quantity still open, entry charges, premium stop and target), kept out of the cash restore, and counted against their underlying's entry for the day. Paper legs in Paper, live legs always. A live one keeps its real-money flag, so its closing order is real in either mode, and sends no order until Kite's day book confirms it is still open (flat in Kite: dropped, no order). An option the engine holds is not an untracked Kite position.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Open option positions lived in memory only, and their entry leg came back as a cash position in the option's tradingsymbol (#187). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/state.py:_rehydrate_fno_positions, _rehydrate_today; backend/database.py:fno_trades_since; backend/trading_engine.py:_verify_live_fno, _check_position_reconciliation, TradingEngine.__init__` |
| **How to check** | activity 'Restored N open F&O position(s) from today's journal after a restart'; 'A LIVE option position is open' at error level |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_fno_restart.py::test_an_open_paper_option_is_restored_as_an_option_not_as_cash, backend/tests/test_fno_restart.py::test_kite_flat_drops_it_and_sends_nothing, backend/tests/test_fno_restart.py::test_reconciliation_verifies_it_and_does_not_call_it_untracked` |
| **Source** | README §110 |

</details>

## Scanner

Which stocks are watched, and the market bias.

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-01</code> <b>Active</b> — When Kite is connected the scanner's prices are live: one Kite quote request gives every stock's last price, NSE's opening price, the day's volume…</summary>

When Kite is connected the scanner's prices are live: one Kite quote request gives every stock's last price, NSE's opening price, the day's volume and its average traded price. When Kite is not connected, or its quotes cannot be read, the scanner uses the delayed feed (yfinance) and the page says so. Daily bars and the bars of earlier sessions always come from yfinance, completed from NSE's files (SCN-21, SCN-25).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | How late the delayed feed runs is not known exactly, and its first bar is not NSE's opening price. On the live session of 2026-09-29 the running scanner's gap was off by 0.3 points or more on 23 of 100 stocks (#193, #196); its last price was not late. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:Scanner.run, fetch_live_quotes, live_day, live_metrics; backend/data_provider.py:kite_quotes` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.live_feed = True` |
| **How to check** | Screener page: 'Prices are live from Kite as of HH:MM'; /api/scanner feed |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_live_feed.py::test_with_kite_connected_the_scan_describes_today_before_the_delayed_feed_has_a_bar` |
| **Source** | README §101 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-02</code> <b>Active</b> — The daily profile uses only sessions strictly before the scan session and needs at least 60 daily bars.</summary>

The daily profile uses only sessions strictly before the scan session and needs at least 60 daily bars. Otherwise the stock is not ranked.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | No look-ahead: the same score must be computable in backtests. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:daily_profile` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner 'scanned' count &lt; 100 when history is short |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_lookahead_proof.py::test_day_T_own_bar_is_excluded_not_merely_the_future` |
| **Source** | README §40 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-03</code> <b>Active</b> — The scanner runs every 5 minutes while the market phase is open or in the square-off window, and every 60 minutes otherwise on a trading day.</summary>

The scanner runs every 5 minutes while the market phase is open or in the square-off window, and every 60 minutes otherwise on a trading day. On a weekend or an NSE holiday it runs once that date: the result updates the plan the dashboard shows, but not the tracked list, and logs no 'Now tracking' / 'Stopped tracking' lines. The first tick after start always scans, and only one scan thread runs at a time; POST /api/scan triggers one manually.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The dashboard shows a plan even while the market is closed. On 2026-10-02..04 (a holiday and a weekend) it ran 44-49 scans a day, one of 4,940 s, and the list churned with nothing able to trade (#259). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:Scanner.due; backend/trading_engine.py:_tick_impl, request_scan, _run_scan, _is_trading_day` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.interval_minutes_open = 5; SCANNER.interval_minutes_closed = 60` |
| **How to check** | scans table ts spacing; activity 'Scanning the NIFTY 100 universe…' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_engine_correctness.py::test_an_off_day_scans_once_and_does_not_change_tracking; backend/tests/test_engine_correctness.py::test_a_trading_day_still_scans_on_its_cadence_and_tracks_the_picks` |
| **Source** | README §2, §122, issue #259 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-04</code> <b>Active</b> — A stock is excluded (AVOID) if its last close is below ₹100, its 20-day average turnover is below ₹50 cr/day, or its daily ATR is below 1.2% of price.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Intraday trades need liquidity and enough range to beat costs. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:tradability_exclusion` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.min_price = 100; SCANNER.min_turnover_cr = 50; SCANNER.min_atr_pct = 1.2` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner rows with status AVOID and excluded text; scan_rows.excluded |
| **Source** | README §2 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-05</code> <b>Active</b> — A stock with results due today or on the next trading day (NSE event calendar; the next day that is not a weekend or an NSE holiday), or with an…</summary>

A stock with results due today or on the next trading day (NSE event calendar; the next day that is not a weekend or an NSE holiday), or with an ex-date today (NSE corporate actions), is excluded from new trades.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Event risk; an ex-date gap is mechanical, not a signal. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:Scanner.run; backend/nse_feed.py:results_calendar, corporate_actions_on; backend/holidays.py:next_trading_day` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner rows with excluded '... — event risk, no new trades' or 'Ex-date today' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_holiday_calendar.py::test_results_after_a_holiday_are_excluded_on_the_day_before_it` |
| **Source** | README §2, §20, §114 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-06</code> <b>Active</b> — Every stock is scored once as a long and once as a mirrored short (as a long only when it is long-only or SCANNER.allow_shorts is off).</summary>

Every stock is scored once as a long and once as a mirrored short (as a long only when it is long-only or SCANNER.allow_shorts is off). The stronger is kept as the row's score_side, with long_score and short_score, for information only. The row's side is empty: the scanner sets no side, and nothing that gates or sizes an entry reads score_side. The Jev book reads it as its registered baseline (JEV-11), and the old 'score' selection mode still ranks by it (SCN-08).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The old score's rank IC was 0.000 over 434 sessions and −0.0021 over 436 (README §37, §52). The scanner audit found no stage of the funnel with a measured edge and said the old score should no longer set the side (rule 3.8). It is kept visible so the page still says what it reads. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:Scanner.run; backend/trading_engine.py:_entry_block_reason` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.allow_shorts = True` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner rows: side null, score_side, long_score, short_score; Screener rows carry no Long/Short pill |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_the_scan_sets_no_side_and_keeps_the_old_scores_lean_for_information, backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_a_long_only_stock_has_no_short_score` |
| **Source** | README §2, §115 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-07</code> <b>Active</b> — The stocks on the day's list get a full Sahab's Dimaag read with per-stock news and fundamentals on finished bars.</summary>

The stocks on the day's list get a full Sahab's Dimaag read with per-stock news and fundamentals on finished bars. That read adjusts the score by 2 × the bull-bear edge signed by score_side, clamped to ±15, to give final_score. In 'liquidity' mode final_score is shown but does not choose the list.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Rank shortlisted names on the same evidence the entry logic uses. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:Scanner.run` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.deep_analysis = 25` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner rows: brain non-null and final_score != score for the top 25 |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_selection.py::test_the_most_traded_eligible_stocks_are_chosen_whatever_their_score_or_side` |
| **Source** | README §2, §25 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-08</code> <b>Retired</b> — Retired as the default on 2026-09-28: the active list was the 25 best rows by final_score, skipping rows below 20 or whose daily trend fought their…</summary>

Retired as the default on 2026-09-28: the active list was the 25 best rows by final_score, skipping rows below 20 or whose daily trend fought their side, with at most 2 picks against the market bias, re-chosen every scan. Still available with SCANNER['selection'] = 'score'.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Its ranking was measured to carry no information (README §37, §52), and it rotated 51 stocks through the list in one session, so only 10 were watched long enough for the order-book test (README §91). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:select_active` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.selection = 'score' restores it` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner active, active_sides; rows status ACTIVE |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_selection.py::test_liquidity_is_the_default_and_score_mode_is_still_available` |
| **Source** | README §91 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-14</code> <b>Active</b> — The day's list is the 25 eligible stocks with the highest 20-day average turnover, most-traded first.</summary>

The day's list is the 25 eligible stocks with the highest 20-day average turnover, most-traded first. No score, side, trend or checklist read enters the choice.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | No scanner ranking has been shown to predict intraday returns, so the list is chosen for what can be measured: the most-traded names have the tightest spreads (median 1.0 bp against 2.5 bp for the least-traded third on 2026-09-28). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:select_liquid; backend/scanner.py:Scanner.run` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.selection = 'liquidity'; SCANNER.active_count = 25` |
| **How to check** | Screener page, Trading tab: the rule is printed above the list; GET /api/scanner returns selection.mode = 'liquidity' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_selection.py::test_the_most_traded_eligible_stocks_are_chosen_whatever_their_score_or_side` |
| **Source** | README §91 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-15</code> <b>Active</b> — The day's list is fixed before the open, at the first pre-market read at or after 08:45 on a trading day, and kept all day, a restart included…</summary>

The day's list is fixed before the open, at the first pre-market read at or after 08:45 on a trading day, and kept all day, a restart included (SCN-24). A stock that stops being eligible later in the day is dropped, not replaced, so the list only shrinks. If no read ran before the open, the first scan with data for at least 90% of the universe fixes it, and the page says so.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A stable list lets every watched stock be observed for the whole session, which the order-book test needs, and stops the review queue and the Jev book from seeing a different set of stocks every few minutes. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:Scanner.fix_day_list and day_list_for; backend/trading_engine.py:should_fix_list and _fix_day_list` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.fix_list_from = "08:45"; SCANNER.freeze_min_coverage = 0.9` |
| **How to check** | Screener page: 'Fixed before the open at HH:MM'; /api/scanner selection.fixed_when |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_a_list_fixed_before_the_open_is_the_days_list` |
| **Source** | README §91, §100 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-16</code> <b>Active</b> — The pre-market read chooses its watchlist by the same rule, so the morning list and the day's list are the same stocks.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The watchlist seeded before the open should not change when the first live scan runs. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:run_premarket` |
| **How to check** | Pre-Market page: the 'On today's list' stocks match the Screener's Trading tab |
| **Source** | README §91 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-17</code> <b>Active</b> — A stock on NSE's F&amp;O ban list for the day is left alone: it is excluded from the day's list and from new trades.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A stock enters the ban when market-wide derivative positions pass 95% of the limit. Positioning is crowded and its futures cannot take new positions. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:guard_check; backend/nse_feed.py:fno_ban_list` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.guards = True` |
| **How to check** | Screener page, the line under the intro; Skipped tab shows the reason |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_a_stock_in_the_ban_is_left_alone` |
| **Source** | README §100; NSE fo_secban.csv |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-18</code> <b>Active</b> — A stock with a fixed price band is long-only: it is never scored or traded as a short.</summary>

A stock with a fixed price band is long-only: it is never scored or traded as a short. It is left alone when its price is within 2% of either band. On live prices the band is the exchange's own limit for the day; otherwise it is worked out from the previous close. Stocks with derivatives have no fixed band and are not affected.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A short caught at the upper band cannot be covered, and an order at a locked band does not fill. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:guard_check; backend/nse_feed.py:price_bands` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.near_band_pct = 2.0` |
| **How to check** | Screener page: 'Long only' on ENRIN, TATACAP and TMCV (2026-09-29) |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_a_banded_stock_near_its_band_is_left_alone` |
| **Source** | README §100; NSE sec_list.csv |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-19</code> <b>Active</b> — A stock in trade-for-trade (series BE or BZ) or carrying a graded-surveillance remark in NSE's price-band list is left alone.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A trade-for-trade position cannot be squared off the same day, so it cannot be an intraday trade. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:guard_check` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.guards = True` |
| **How to check** | Skipped tab shows the reason |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_a_stock_in_trade_for_trade_or_under_surveillance_is_left_alone` |
| **Source** | README §100; NSE sec_list.csv |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-20</code> <b>Active</b> — A guard file that cannot be fetched or read is unknown, not empty: it excludes nothing, and the page says it could not be read, when the last try…</summary>

A guard file that cannot be fetched or read is unknown, not empty: it excludes nothing, and the page says it could not be read, when the last try failed and when NSE is asked again. A failed fetch (no answer, a refusal or an unreadable file) is remembered per file for 180 s: until then a caller gets 'unknown' at once instead of another 15 s timeout, and a stale good copy is not returned in its place.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Showing 'no stock is banned' when the list was never read would be a false statement. Without the memory, every caller waited out its own timeout while NSE was down: four F&O candidates took 60 s, now 15 s (#212). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/nse_feed.py:_archive, last_failure, failure_text, parse_fno_ban, parse_price_bands; backend/scanner.py:load_guards, guards_summary` |
| **Setting** | `nse_feed.ARCHIVE_RETRY_S = 180, ARCHIVE_TIMEOUT_S = 15` |
| **How to check** | Screener page: 'could not be read (the last try, at …, failed: …; tried again after …)'; backend log 'NSE F&O ban list unavailable (…); not asked for again for 180 s' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_unknown_files_exclude_nothing; backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_a_failed_fetch_is_not_retried_until_the_retry_time; backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_the_failure_says_when_and_why_and_the_file_stays_unknown; backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_the_scan_says_when_an_unread_guard_file_last_failed` |
| **Source** | README §100, §111 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-21</code> <b>Active</b> — When the daily bars do not hold the last completed session, it is added from NSE's equity bhavcopy and index closing file.</summary>

When the daily bars do not hold the last completed session, it is added from NSE's equity bhavcopy and index closing file. The session is looked for by date, so it is added in its place when the bars already end with today's. If that fails, the pre-market read says which session it ranked on.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The delayed feed's daily bars end a session early for hours after the close, so a read before the open ranked on data one session old (#192). During the next session they can carry today's bar and still lack yesterday's: 16 of 100 stocks on 2026-09-29 (#196). |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:complete_daily; backend/nse_feed.py:last_session` |
| **How to check** | Pre-market page: 'Ranked on the &lt;date> close'; /api/premarket result.daily |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_guards.py::test_a_missing_last_session_is_added_and_nothing_else_is_touched` |
| **Source** | README §100 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-22</code> <b>Active</b> — On live prices, relative volume is the day's volume so far against the average volume traded by the same minute of the day over the earlier sessions…</summary>

On live prices, relative volume is the day's volume so far against the average volume traded by the same minute of the day over the earlier sessions in the 5-minute bars. With no earlier session to compare with, it is left blank.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | A quote gives the day's volume to the second. The yardstick has to be measured at the same time of day to mean anything. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:volume_curve, expected_volume, live_metrics` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner rows: rvol near 1 on an ordinary day |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_live_feed.py::test_live_metrics_read_the_gap_from_nses_open_and_volume_against_the_curve` |
| **Source** | README §101 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-23</code> <b>Active</b> — The stocks on the day's list get live 5-minute bars for their checklist read.</summary>

The stocks on the day's list get live 5-minute bars for their checklist read. The other stocks keep the delayed bars, which are used only for their opening range and their volume yardstick.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | 25 requests a scan is a small share of Kite's budget; 100 would crowd the engine's own requests. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:Scanner.run` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.deep_analysis = 25` |
| **How to check** | /api/candles/&lt;symbol> for a listed stock ends on the current bar |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_live_feed.py::test_the_days_list_gets_live_bars_and_with_them_its_opening_range` |
| **Source** | README §101 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-24</code> <b>Active</b> — The day's list survives a restart.</summary>

The day's list survives a restart. It is written to the journal when it is fixed and read back when the backend starts. A list already fixed for the session is used as it is, with the time it was first fixed and how; the first list written for a session stands. A list for an earlier session is not reused. After a restart the engine watches the list from the first tick, and the ordinary pre-market read does not seed another.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The list was held in memory only, so a restart chose it again: the restart of 2026-09-29 at 18:08 put HINDALCO in place of TVSMOTOR (#198). The watchdog restarts a backend that stops answering, so a restart inside a session is expected. The engine, the order-book sampler and Jev's round would each have seen a different list part-way through the day. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/database.py:record_day_list, get_day_list, latest_day_list; backend/scanner.py:Scanner._stored_list and _keep; backend/trading_engine.py:_restore_day_list and _maybe_seed_watchlist_from_premarket` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.selection = 'liquidity'` |
| **How to check** | After a restart in a session: the Screener still reads 'Fixed before the open at HH:MM' with the first time; the activity log says the list was read back from the journal; the journal's day_lists table has one row for the session |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_day_list_restart.py::test_a_restarted_scanner_keeps_the_list_and_the_time_it_was_fixed; backend/tests/test_day_list_restart.py::test_the_engines_pre_open_fix_is_written_and_a_restarted_engine_watches_it; backend/tests/test_scanner_live_feed.py::test_after_a_restart_the_scan_keeps_the_list_and_the_time_it_was_fixed` |
| **Source** | README §106 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-25</code> <b>Active</b> — A stock's score gets +6 when its industry's real NSE sector index is in a daily uptrend or downtrend (close, EMA20 and EMA50 in order) on the side of…</summary>

A stock's score gets +6 when its industry's real NSE sector index is in a daily uptrend or downtrend (close, EMA20 and EMA50 in order) on the side of the trade, and −6 against it. The trend needs 51 daily bars before the session. When the delayed feed gives an index fewer, its history is built from NSE's index closing files for the last 60 sessions, NSE's bar kept where both have one. Each file is downloaded once and kept; NSE is asked once a day, at most 60 files a day, half a second apart, and a pass that missed a session is tried again after an hour. An industry whose trend still cannot be worked out is listed in the scan result as sector_trends_unavailable and named on the Screener.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Since 2026-09-16 the delayed feed has served one daily bar for six of the eight sector indices, and the check was skipped without a word for 61 of the 100 stocks (#197). On 60 bars EMA50 has not fully settled: for IT and Pharma, April to September 2026, the label matched the one from a year of bars on 265 of 275 days. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:intraday_score, complete_sector_history; backend/sectoral_indices.py:sector_trend, complete_from_nse; backend/nse_feed.py:index_history` |
| **Setting** | `nse_feed.INDEX_HISTORY_SESSIONS = 60, INDEX_HISTORY_MAX_DOWNLOADS = 60` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner sector_trends_unavailable is empty and sector_history_from_nse names the indices built from NSE's files; the Screener shows no 'Sector trend unavailable' line |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_sector_index_history.py::test_a_scan_takes_the_trend_from_nses_history_and_names_what_it_could_not_work_out` |
| **Source** | README §107 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-26</code> <b>Active</b> — Every scan journals every stock it read, with the inputs of the scanner audit's passes 1 to 3.</summary>

Every scan journals every stock it read, with the inputs of the scanner audit's passes 1 to 3. In scan_rows: the list status, exclusion, long-only flag, price feed and the time of the price, last price, change, gap, relative volume, VWAP, opening range, the average change of the other stocks in its industry, its sector index's daily trend, turnover, ATR %, the old score (score, long_score, short_score, score_side) and the shadow direction of audit rule 3.8. In scans: the feed, the quote time, the NIFTY's price, open, change and daily trend, VIX and FII net. The shadow direction is LONG when the stock is above its VWAP, ahead of its industry and the NIFTY is above its open (an index has no VWAP), SHORT when all three are down, and empty otherwise; nothing that trades reads it. At the first tick of the 15:08 square-off window, Kite's last traded price of every universe stock and the NIFTY is written once a session to session_closes, never a delayed price; without Kite nothing is written and the log says so once. The view scan_candidates joins them: every stock of every scan with its inputs and its return in bp from the scan's price to the 15:08 price, empty for a scan after 15:08 or a session without a close.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | The audit's rule 5.3: without a log of every stock at each stage and its return to 15:08, nobody can say whether a pass helped. Its section 6 runs passes 1 to 3 in shadow, placing no orders, so a later pre-registered look at gap, time-of-day relative volume, VWAP distance and sector strength can read the inputs without reconstructing them. The columns extend the rows already written for every stock of every scan, so nothing is stored twice. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/database.py:record_scan, record_session_closes, scan_candidates, _migrate; backend/scanner.py:shadow_side; backend/scanner.py:Scanner.run; backend/trading_engine.py:_record_session_closes` |
| **How to check** | sqlite: SELECT \* FROM scan_candidates WHERE session_date = '&lt;date>'; activity 'Shadow log: recorded the 15:08 price of N stocks and indices' |
| **Test** | `backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_every_stock_of_every_scan_is_journaled_with_its_inputs_and_scored_at_1508, backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_the_1508_prices_are_read_from_kite_once_a_session, backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_the_shadow_direction_needs_all_three_legs_to_agree, backend/tests/test_scanner_side_shadow_log.py::test_a_journal_from_before_gains_the_columns_and_its_rows_read_the_old_side` |
| **Source** | README §115; docs/research/scanner-audit-2026-09-28.md (rules 3.8, 5.3, section 6) |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-09</code> <b>Active</b> — Market bias is scored from the NIFTY trend, its day change (±0.3%), holding above the open, universe breadth (≥60% / ≤40%), VIX ≥ 20 and FII net flow…</summary>

Market bias is scored from the NIFTY trend, its day change (±0.3%), holding above the open, universe breadth (≥60% / ≤40%), VIX ≥ 20 and FII net flow (±₹1,000 cr). A score ≥ 2 is risk-on and ≤ −2 is risk-off. When VIX ≥ 20, new position sizes are multiplied by 0.5.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Varsity/Murphy market context decides which side gets the slots. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:market_context; backend/trading_engine.py:_run_scan` |
| **Setting** | `MARKET_FILTER.vix_high = 20.0; MARKET_FILTER.vix_high_size_multiplier = 0.5` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner market.bias, score, reasons; activity 'India VIX ... elevated — new position sizes reduced' |
| **Source** | README §1 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-10</code> <b>Active</b> — TRIN (whole-exchange breadth), the Union Budget-day note, and bulk/block deals are shown as context and never add points.</summary>

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Not yet validated by IC; bulk-deal 'edge' is explained by leakage in the literature. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/scanner.py:market_context; backend/nse_feed.py:large_deals_today` |
| **How to check** | /api/scanner market.reasons '(informational, not scored)'; rows large_deals |
| **Source** | README §20, §18 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-11</code> <b>Active</b> — The engine's watchlist is pinned symbols, then the scanner's active picks, then symbols with an open position, de-duplicated in that order.</summary>

The engine's watchlist is pinned symbols, then the scanner's active picks, then symbols with an open position, de-duplicated in that order. It is rebuilt after every scan; in 'liquidity' mode the active picks stay the same all session.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Held positions must stay watched for stops and square-off. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_run_scan; backend/app.py:set_watchlist` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.pinned = []` |
| **How to check** | /api/state watchlist; activity 'Now tracking' / 'Stopped tracking' |
| **Source** | README §2 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-12</code> <b>Active</b> — The pre-market ranking (daily bars only, before today) runs once per IST day on the first engine tick, holidays included.</summary>

The pre-market ranking (daily bars only, before today) runs once per IST day on the first engine tick, holidays included. It also re-runs from GET /api/premarket when the result is more than 30 minutes old. It seeds the watchlist at most once a day, only on a trading day, and only if no live scan has run yet that day.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Be watching a real shortlist from the open without fighting the live scanner. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/trading_engine.py:_tick_impl, _maybe_seed_watchlist_from_premarket; backend/app.py:get_premarket` |
| **Setting** | `SCANNER.active_count = 25 (shortlist size)` |
| **How to check** | GET /api/premarket result.watchlist; activity 'Pre-market shortlist seeded: ...' |
| **Source** | README §14, §122, issue #259 |

</details>

<details>
<summary><code>SCN-13</code> <b>Active</b> — The universe is the NIFTY 100 from backend/data/nifty100.csv.</summary>

The universe is the NIFTY 100 from backend/data/nifty100.csv. It is re-downloaded from NSE archives when the file is more than 7 days old, and the download is accepted only if it parses to at least 50 rows. An empty universe makes the scan fail.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Work offline, but don't overwrite a good list with a broken download. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/universe.py:load` |
| **Setting** | `universe.REFRESH_SECONDS = 604800` |
| **How to check** | stat backend/data/nifty100.csv mtime; /api/scanner scanned ≈ 100 |
| **Source** | README §21 |

</details>

## Market data

Where prices come from and what happens when a source fails.

<details>
<summary><code>DAT-01</code> <b>Active</b> — Kite is used for market data only when USE_KITE_DATA is true, an API key and access token are present, and that exact token has not already been…</summary>

Kite is used for market data only when USE_KITE_DATA is true, an API key and access token are present, and that exact token has not already been rejected by Kite. Otherwise data comes from yfinance.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Why** | Stop hammering a dead session every tick. |
| **Enforced in** | `backend/data_provider.py:kite_data_active` |
| **Setting** | `USE_KITE_DATA = True` |
